transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Sanjay (Redwood AE), Renee (Redwood SE), Marta (ClearLedger Head of Search), Owen (Infra Eng), Priya (SecOps)

Summary: Privacy-sensitive FinTech search team evaluating hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC) for embeddings + rerank pipeline. Primary concerns: data residency, KMS/keys, throughput at 800-1200 QPS fanout, embedding dimensionality tradeoffs (384 vs 768), hybrid search vs rerank cost model, and integration with customer's existing vector DB (self-hosted Milvus-ish cluster). Decided pilot: 10M docs, 2-tier routing (fast cache + rerank on Redwood Hosted/Dedicated), with security docs and pricing follow-up.

Topics: hosting modes, private VPC control plane, KMS/HSM, RBAC + audit logs, embedding dims and quantization, batch vs real-time inference, prefetched KV caching, vector DB sharding and fallback, cost vs latency tradeoffs, pilot success criteria

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00:00] Sanjay (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros from Redwood side — I'm Sanjay, AE, and Renee is our solutions engineer.
[00:00:10] Renee (SE): Hi all, Renee Walker. I focus on embeddings performance and infra integration.
[00:00:18] Marta (ClearLedger): Marta Li, I run search and relevance at ClearLedger. we're evaluating options for embedding store and rerank.
[00:00:22] Owen (ClearLedger): Owen Grant, infra engineering, i'll care about network topology and private-hosting requirements.
[00:00:26] Priya (ClearLedger): Priya Shah, SecOps — will look at KMS, logs, and compliance.
[00:00:32] Sanjay: Great. Goal for today is to understand your constraints and walk through reachable pilot configs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. we'll cover perf numbers, security, and integration points with your vector DB.

[00:02:05] Marta: Quick context — we are a regulated payments platform, so PII and transaction metadata are sensitive. We want to run most inference in a private tenancy but keep options open for hybrid because of cost. Our current search stack is an in-house vector service built from Milvus 2.x patterns, sharded across 8 nodes; we do synchronous rerank with a 768-d embedding today. Latency target is 95th < 120ms for the user-facing path, ideally 80ms.

[00:03:10] Owen: Also want to avoid egressing unredacted transaction text. encryption keys must be under our control where possible.

[00:04:00] Renee: Understood. Redwood offers three main operating modes — Hosted API (fastest onboarding), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools you control via config, predictable throughput), and Private (VPC + on-prem or customer-managed control plane). For private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and keep the inference inside your VPC.

[00:04:32] Priya: On KMS — we need envelope encryption with our cloud KMS and key rotation logs. Is that supported in Private?
[00:04:40] Renee: Yes, private deployments support customer-managed KMS and we can hook into your key rotation and audit logs. There are some config items around tokenization and secret push; we'll share the security pack with exact capabilities. (link to security pack: https://redwood.example/security-pack)

[00:05:12] Marta: Good. Now about throughput — day-to-day peak for search fanout is around 800 QPS, with occasional spikes to 1.2k. Most queries fanout ~32 docs for embed recall, then rerank top 10 with a cross-encoder. We want to explore moving rerank to Redwood but keep vector store in-house initially.

[00:05:48] Renee: Makes sense. Two approaches we usually see: 1) host embeddings generation and rerank on Redwood and keep vector DB in your network (we call this hybrid routing), or 2) export embeddings and host both retrieval and rerank in your infra with Redwood only providing model variants. The former reduces egress and centralizes rerank SLAs.

[00:06:10] Owen: If we keep vector DB in our VPC, what's the network pattern? do you reach into our VPC or does data leave to Redwood?

[00:06:25] Sanjay: In Private mode we install the inference nodes in your VPC or on-prem — nothing leaves. In Dedicated you get isolated GPU pools but it's still a Redwood-managed tenancy; certain metadata and control-plane signals go to Redwood. For Hosted, everything runs in Redwood's cloud and you'd have to redaction/transform sensitive fields before sending.

[00:07:02] Priya: We need audit logs and SSO — SAML or OIDC integration is required and we need to demonstrate SOC2 controls.
[00:07:12] Renee: We have SAML SSO and RBAC; we'll attach per-route audit logs and token-level traces in the Console. We'll include our SOC2 and ISO docs in the pack.

[00:08:00] Marta: Let's talk embedding dims — we currently use 768-d embeddings. Did you see large quality drop moving to 384-d?

[00:08:15] Renee: It depends on signal and downstream rerank. For many tabular or transactional retrievals 384 dims with a strong reranker can match 768 for top-k. The advantage is throughput and storage; 384-d halves memory and accelerates similarity. We can run a small eval: 384 vs 768 on a held-out set. For latency, 384 reduces compute on GPU inference and vector DB distance ops.

[00:09:05] Owen: If we quantize to int8 or 4-bit, are there Redwood-recommended quant profiles for embeddings?

[00:09:15] Renee: For embeddings we typically suggest FP16 or 8-bit float quant for generator models. For pure vector space storage, post-hoc product quantization or OPQ in the vector DB is more common; Redwood supports model-side lower-precision exports but we test for quality regressions. We'll include quantization guidance.

[00:10:00] [background noise] Speaker 1 (maybe a connection hiccup)

[00:10:30] Marta: on cost — can you ballpark cost of running rerank at 1k QPS? we need a rough unit econ to compare to hosting ourselves.

[00:10:45] Sanjay: quick rough: depends on model size and batching — if you run a small cross-encoder optimized for GPU with batching and prefix caching, cost per 1k QPS is in the mid-range; we'll provide a detailed cost simulation. For Dedicated we can reduce unit cost with reserved capacity and autoscale. I'll follow up with a pricing deck that shows reserved vs on-demand.

[00:11:30] Priya: Any data retention policy for logs and raw requests? must be configurable and possible to set to zero retention for payloads.

[00:11:40] Renee: Yes, for Private you can opt out of request retention. For Hosted we provide retention controls and encryption; again we'll send the specifics.

[00:12:20] Marta: technical integration: we want to keep current Milvus cluster. what's the integration pattern for rerank? we could either stream top-K IDs to Redwood or proxy queries through Redwood which hits our vector DB.

[00:12:38] Renee: both are supported. Common no-egress pattern: you run an internal adapter that streams top-k doc ids and their embeddings (or context) to Redwood over a secure tunnel, Redwood performs the cross-encoder rerank inside your VPC if private, or in Dedicated if you accept data plane managed by Redwood. Another pattern is to run the reranker inside your infra as a Redwood-managed container image if you want control — that's our private on-prem package option.

[00:13:25] Owen: If we stream embeddings, does Redwood store them? we want ephemeral only.

[00:13:32] Renee: We can configure ephemeral cache only and disable persistent storage in Private. For Hosted we'd avoid storing raw doc text by design; embeddings can be kept transient if you require.

[00:14:10] Marta: ok interesting. about tail latency — our main concern is 95th. what mechanisms help keep tail down?

[00:14:20] Renee: continuous batching, prioritized routing, prefix KV caching, and on-the-fly fallback to smaller models. We also do request-level shaping and can pin a pool for low-latency traffic. For vector DB fanout we often recommend a two-stage approach: a cheap approximate first-pass (HNSW/quantized) then neural rerank for top-k. That reduces PS latency and cost.

[00:15:00] Marta: our rerank is costly — we might shift to using a smaller cross-encoder only for candidate sets below 32. can Redwood handle hybrid rules like that?

[00:15:12] Renee: Absolutely — you can configure per-route policies that say: for top-5 prefer model A, for >5 and <50 prefer cheap model B then fallback to full reranker for top-10. We call that routing policies + model variants.

[00:16:05] Priya: about audit and compliance again — do you support customer-managed logging endpoints (push to our SIEM)?

[00:16:14] Renee: Yes, we support shipping audit logs to your S3, CloudWatch, or GCS, and can push to a SIEM via secure forwarder. We'll map the fields in the pack.

[00:17:00] Owen: network ports and egress — if we set up Private, what's the install footprint and resource needs?

[00:17:12] Renee: For a Private deployment to handle 1k QPS rerank at 768-d, rough starting point is a small GPU cluster with 4x A10/A30-equivalents with autoscale headroom; we can reduce GPUs with smaller dims. We will provide a sizing worksheet. For Dedicated you can achieve similar with reserved pools but plan for network NAT and control-plane connectivity.

[00:18:05] Marta: can we do a pilot where we keep vector DB in our VPC and run rerank in Redwood Dedicated to evaluate quality and costs?

[00:18:15] Sanjay: Yes — that's a common pilot. We'd do a 4-week pilot with 10M docs, baseline metrics, throughput runbook, and a bench with your sample data. We'll instrument 95th, p99, and token/eval cost.

[00:19:00] Owen: for the bench, do you need full documents or just embeddings and ground truth labels?

[00:19:08] Renee: Ideally we need embeddings for retrieval simulation and labeled pairs for rerank evals. If you can't share raw text, an anonymized set or hash pointers plus embeddings works.

[00:20:00] Marta: timeline — we have board review mid-April; can we get pilot results by early April?

[00:20:10] Sanjay: tight but doable: kickoff this week, bench week 1-2, run pilot week 3-4, preliminary results end of week 4. we'll need your dataset and infra details ASAP.

[00:21:05] Priya: any known limits around private deployment and our compliance? for ex, network egress logs and KMS attestation?

[00:21:15] Renee: we have KMS integrations and can produce attestation reports; some enterprise items require an on-site checklist but we'll work through SOC2 artifacts.

[00:22:50] Marta: can you speak to failure modes — what happens when a GPU pool is saturated during spikes?

[00:23:00] Renee: Redwood has fallback policies — you can fallback to a smaller model, route to dedicated fallback pool, or temporarily increase batching which trades latency for throughput. For mission-critical routes pinning low-latency capacity is recommended.

[00:23:45] Owen: about vector DB reconciliation — if we do partial/hybrid flows, will you help instrument consistency checks for embeddings and payload offsets?

[00:23:55] Renee: yes, we provide sync scripts and a small reconciliation harness to detect drift between stored embeddings and model outputs — especially important if you regenerate embeddings with upgraded models.

[00:25:10] [short pause]

[00:25:45] Marta: can Redwood do a head-to-head with our current in-house reranker? we want apples-to-apples latency/accuracy.

[00:25:58] Renee: We'll run a bench using your labeled set and run both the current reranker and Redwood-managed variants. we'll deliver precision/recall curves and cost per query numbers.

[00:26:40] Sanjay: I'll attach a pricing/architecture deck after the call (pricing deck link: https://redwood.example/pricing-dedicated).

[00:27:25] Priya: around encryption in transit — do you use mTLS to backend vector DBs?

[00:27:32] Renee: yes mutual TLS is supported for all control plane and data plane connections in Private. For Dedicated we use TLS plus VPN peering options.

[00:28:10] Marta: slight question: we sometimes see noisy neighbors when using shared services — how strict is isolation in Dedicated?

[00:28:18] Renee: Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools per customer and resource reservations. It's not the same as Private (customer-managed infra) but it gives strong isolation in the Redwood fabric.

[00:29:00] Owen: trying to be pragmatic — for pilot which route gives fastest time to signal while meeting our data constraints?

[00:29:10] Sanjay: Probably Dedicated with VPC peering to keep the vector DB in your network and rerank in Dedicated. That way data plane can be proxied and minimal payloads forwarded. If you need absolute no-egress, Private is the choice but has longer setup.

[00:30:22] Marta: can we try a small smoke test on Hosted to validate quality before spinning up Dedicated?

[00:30:30] Renee: You can do an eval on Hosted with synthetic or redacted data to get a quality baseline quickly. Then we can move to Dedicated or Private for compliance and perf.

[00:31:05] Priya: for legal, do you have a data processing addendum and standard contract terms for SOC2 customers?

[00:31:12] Sanjay: Yes we'll share our DPA and standard enterprise terms. we can involve legal on both sides in the next week.

[00:32:40] Marta: question on rerank model lifecycle — if we update model weights, how do we avoid drift in production retrieval relevance?

[00:32:50] Renee: Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals against your golden prompt set and trigger regressions. Also we do canary rollouts and model version pinning so you can rollback quickly.

[00:33:30] Owen: any examples of customers with similar scale using Private?

[00:33:38] Renee: we have a few fintech customers; i'll follow up with anonymized case studies.

[00:34:10] [audio artifact] Speaker 2: (mumble)

[00:34:50] Marta: ok let's lock down pilot scope then: 10M docs, vector DB stays in our VPC, rerank runs in Dedicated initially, evaluate 384 vs 768 dims, cost simulation, and SOC2/security review.

[00:35:10] Sanjay: sounds right. rough milestones: 1) Security screen (this week) 2) dataset & infra details (by 03-06) 3) bench + quality eval (03-09 to 03-13) 4) pilot run (03-16 to 04-10) 5) results & board pack (by 04-14).

[00:36:00] Renee: I'll prepare a throughput worksheet and run the throughput estimate. also will include recommended quant profiles and batching knobs.

[00:36:30] Priya: please send the SOC2/email chain and the list of supporting artifacts we need for legal review.

[00:36:40] Sanjay: will do.

[00:37:20] Marta: small question — for the hybrid flow, do you support warmed KV cache for frequent prefixes to reduce cost?

[00:37:30] Renee: yes Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching; you can configure TTLs and warm frequently-hit keys, which can significantly reduce per-query compute.

[00:38:05] Owen: operationally who manages the model updates in Dedicated? can we push model images?

[00:38:12] Renee: In Dedicated you can request model variants and we support pinned versions. For Private you get more direct control and can run our container images with your orchestration. We'll map the admin flows.

[00:39:00] Marta: what telemetry do you emit for operator-level observability? we need token-level cost, latency per route, and per-model histograms.

[00:39:12] Renee: the Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, p95/p99 histograms, traces, and a tracing hook integration for our customers. We'll include sample dashboards.

[00:40:20] [short brainstorming exchange about storage sharding]

[00:41:00] Marta: final ask on accuracy — we'll want PR and Recall at k=10 and k=50; can Redwood compute that as part of bench?

[00:41:10] Renee: yes we'll produce precision/recall curves and MAP; and show per-dim tradeoffs between 384 and 768.
